name: Rathmoley
agent: Jonathan Gleeson, Sherry FitzGerald Gleeson, Thurles
questions: What is the heating system and its age (electric underfloor downstairs?), and what do running costs look like? Could the front lawn be fenced for dogs?

Behind the rear stone wall the aerials show a neighbouring holding: vegetable plots, a long shed and what looks like a sand arena about 75 m from the house, and a house about 100 m south-east. Whose is it, what is it used for (horses, livestock, a business), and is there any planning on it? BuyerIQ lists 5 applications within 1 km, one an active build.

Could Bedroom 5 (3.17 × 2.76 m, en-suite with shower) and the playroom next to it (3.44 × 5.85 m, with kitchen units, a stove and its own outside door) be used as a parents' annex as they are, and would any planning or building-regulation sign-off be needed? Is the boundary around the patio outside that door dog-proof?

The brochure gives two sets of room labels and sizes: the second calls the ground-floor bedroom 'Bedroom 4', gives the sunroom as 3.42 × 8.13 m and the playroom as 3.33 m wide. Can you confirm the Giraffe360 plan (sunroom 3.42 × 5.85 m) is correct, and when was the house built?

Heating is electric underfloor on the ground floor plus solid-fuel stoves with a back boiler. What heats the first floor when the stoves are out, and what were the last 12 months' electricity and fuel bills?

What is the drainage: a septic tank or a treatment unit, how old, and is it registered? Which supply feeds the house, mains or the private well? Is fibre broadband connected (BuyerIQ shows about 100 Mb full fibre), and has a radon test been done?

ai.why: A sound 225 m² stone-fronted house with big common rooms, three full bathrooms and a genuine ground-floor annex (en-suite bedroom plus a kitchenette playroom with its own door) on 1.31 ac at €475k, 20–25 min from Thurles trains. Held back by about 30 min to the ED in Clonmel, a neighbouring yard 45–100 m behind the rear wall, and a small 8.7 m² parents' bedroom. Held at 3.0 (like Cappoge Lodge): the neighbouring yard ~45 m behind the rear wall and ~30 min to the ED offset the extra bathroom and annex.

electricity.detail: Likely mains; not stated, but a lived-in house with electric underfloor heating.

water.detail: Mains; the brochure says mains water, plus a private well on site.

sewer.detail: Likely septic; not stated, rural site with no public sewer in the townland. Ask its type, age and registration.

internet.detail: Likely fibre; not in the listing. BuyerIQ shows '101 Mb full fibre' in one place and 'no data' in another. Check the Eircode on nbi.ie.

groundFloorBedroom.detail: Bedroom 5 (3.17 × 2.76 m) is on the ground floor with its own shower en-suite, off a corridor that opens into the 3.44 × 5.85 m playroom with kitchen units, a stove and an outside door; the brochure pitches the pair as a granny-flat annex. The room itself is small for a couple.

bedsNote: Four bedrooms upstairs (one now a dressing room with en-suite, easily reinstated) plus en-suite Bedroom 5 on the ground floor
heating: Electric underfloor heating on the ground floor; solid-fuel stoves in the sitting room, living area and playroom, one with a back boiler
tagline: A stone-fronted five-bed country house of 225 m² with a ground-floor annex, big outbuildings and 1.31 elevated acres, about 2.5 km south-west of Killenaule.

pros.detail: Bedroom 5 (3.17 × 2.76 m) has a shower en-suite and sits beside the 3.44 × 5.85 m playroom, which already has kitchen units, a stove and its own door to the patio, so the parents get a bedroom, sitting room and garden door on one level.

About 93 m² of living space downstairs: a 4.40 × 8.13 m kitchen/dining/living room with a stove, a 4.44 × 3.91 m sitting room with a stone fireplace, a vaulted 3.42 × 5.85 m sunroom with garden doors, and the playroom.

pros.text: Three full bathrooms plus a guest WC
pros.detail: A shower en-suite on each floor and a 2.25 × 2.55 m family bathroom upstairs with a bath and separate shower; 5 bedrooms once the dressing room is reinstated.

pros.text: 1.31 acres with mature trees and stone walls
pros.detail: An elevated site with lawns, mature trees and hedgerows on the west and south, stone-pier entrance, post-and-rail fencing and long views to the hills.
About €2,111/m²; stamp duty about €4,750. Turnkey, so little to spend before moving in.
Thurles, about 17 km in a straight line, is on the Cork–Dublin main line with at least 12 departures a day towards Heuston on the current NTA timetable, roughly 1 h 30 to Dublin.
An 87.8 m² detached garage/shed (6.43 × 9.27 m plus a 6.32 × 4.51 m store), a stable block and an older stone outbuilding.
Killenaule has a GP (Killenaule Surgery and the HSE health centre), a Centra, a mixed primary school and Scoil Ruain secondary.

cons.text: The ED is about 30 minutes away
cons.detail: Tipperary University Hospital, Clonmel (all-ages 24-hour ED) is about 22 km in a straight line; Cashel and Thurles are 20+ minutes, so medical care for the parents means a drive.

cons.text: A neighbouring yard behind the rear wall
cons.detail: Satellite and the listing's aerials show a holding south-east with vegetable plots right behind the rear stone wall (~45 m from the house), a long shed and what looks like a sand arena (~75 m) and a house (~100 m), screened only by the wall and a few trees.
Bedroom 5 is 3.17 × 2.76 m (8.7 m²), tight for a double bed and two older people; the playroom next door would have to serve as their sitting room.

Electric underfloor heating downstairs plus three solid-fuel stoves, one with a back boiler; no oil boiler or heat pump is mentioned, so ask how the first floor is heated and what the bills are. BER C1, 155.27 kWh/m²/yr.

cons.text: A two-storey house in the open country
cons.detail: The four main bedrooms are upstairs, and every errand is a 2.5 km drive to Killenaule or 10–15 km to Fethard or Cashel.

cons.text: Local secondary is a small DEIS school
cons.detail: Scoil Ruain (mixed ETB, about 370 pupils) is DEIS; Rockwell College in Cashel (fee-paying) and the Thurles schools are 17+ km away.
Drainage isn't stated (likely septic), broadband isn't in the listing, BuyerIQ flags one locked 'critical' finding, and the brochure's two room schedules disagree on labels and sizes.
